name: Viu
comment: The .viu hybrid container: tag-based <template>/<style>, the C# @script { } block, and the legacy @template/@style blocks kept during the migration window. The authority for this grammar is libraries/Assimalign.Viu.Syntax.SingleFileComponent/docs/FORMAT.md; every rule below is traceable to a section of it. Block bodies delegate to source.cs and source.css rather than re-implementing token rules — the container grammar's job is to slice the file and to own the Viu-specific constructs (interpolations, directive attributes, component tags).

container-comment.comment: FORMAT.md section 2: an HTML comment starting at column 0 is tolerated between blocks and may span lines.
container-comment.name: comment.block.html.viu

script-block.comment: FORMAT.md sections 3 and 3.2: '@script <options> {' opens at column 0 and closes at the FIRST later line whose first column is '}'. That is the container's real termination rule, so the end pattern anchors on '^}' rather than counting braces — a '}' anywhere else on a line is C#, never a closer.
script-block.name: meta.block.script.viu

legacy-template-block.comment: FORMAT.md section 6.1: '@template { }' still parses during the migration window (diagnostic 1015, Warning). Highlighted so a not-yet-migrated file stays readable.
legacy-template-block.name: meta.block.template.legacy.viu

legacy-style-block.comment: FORMAT.md section 6.1: '@style <options> { }' still parses during the migration window (diagnostic 1016, Warning).
legacy-style-block.name: meta.block.style.legacy.viu

custom-block.comment: FORMAT.md section 3: any other '@name { }' is a custom block, preserved verbatim by the parser. Its content has no known language, so only the header is colored.
custom-block.name: meta.block.custom.viu

at-block-options.comment: FORMAT.md section 3.1: valueless flags, or key="value" with no whitespace around '=' and no escape syntax inside the value.

self-closing-block-tag.comment: FORMAT.md section 4: a self-closing <template /> or <style /> is an empty block and opens no content region.

rejected-script-tag-block.comment: FORMAT.md section 6.2: a top-level <script> tag is an ERROR (diagnostic 1017) and contributes no block — a .viu component's C# lives in '@script { }' only. The tag name is scoped invalid so tag-era muscle memory fails visibly in the editor too; the body is left uncolored because it never reaches compilation.
rejected-script-tag-block.name: meta.block.script.rejected.viu

style-tag-block.comment: FORMAT.md sections 4 and 4.1: <style> is raw text to its matching </style>. The body delegates to source.css so the CSS grammar, not a re-implementation, owns declarations, at-rules, and comments.
style-tag-block.name: meta.block.style.viu

template-tag-block.comment: FORMAT.md section 4.1: <template> closes at its MATCHING </template>, so this rule includes itself — a nested <template #header> slot fragment consumes its own closer and cannot end the outer block.
template-tag-block.name: meta.block.template.viu

interpolation.comment: Mustache interpolation. The interior is a C# expression, so it delegates to source.cs; the delimiters keep their own scope so a theme can distinguish them from the expression.
interpolation.name: meta.interpolation.viu

component-tag.comment: A Viu component is named in PascalCase, or as a dotted member expression. Component resolution is ordinal over the authored spelling ([CMP-6]), so casing is a reliable lexical signal and components get their OWN scope rather than borrowing entity.name.tag.

directive-attribute.comment: Directive attributes — 'v-*', the ':' bind shorthand, the '@' event shorthand, and the '#' slot shorthand — carry a C# expression as their value, so the value delegates to source.cs. The end pattern backreferences the opening quote so a value may contain the other quote character and may span lines.

directive-flag.comment: A valueless directive (v-else, v-once, v-pre) has no '=' for the rule above to anchor on.

plain-attribute.comment: An ordinary attribute. 'class' is deliberately NOT split into utility variants and classes here: candidate validation and the generated-CSS preview are language-server features, delivered as semantic tokens and hover rather than guessed lexically.
